facts.text: FMEA (Failure Mode and Effects Analysis), FMECA (Failure Mode, Effects and Criticality Analysis) and FMEDA (Failure Modes, Effects and Diagnostic Analysis) are related table-based methods that examine system parts for possible failures, effects and severity; FMEDA also examines whether the system detects failures.
facts.quote: These are three related table-based methods that go through a system part by part and ask, for each part, how it could fail, what would happen, how serious that would be and, in the FMEDA, whether the system would notice.

facts.text: FMEDA's split into safe and dangerous, detected and undetected failures feeds diagnostic coverage and the probability calculations behind PL, MPL and SIL.

facts.text: The illustrative FMEDA row classifies an open circuit in a radar power connector as dangerous because no detections occur and braking is never commanded.
facts.quote: Radar power connector: open circuit. Effect: no detections. System effect: brake never commanded. Dangerous.

facts.text: The illustrative radar power connector failure is detected by loss of heartbeat within 500 milliseconds, after which the machine fails to safe.
facts.quote: Detected by loss of heartbeat within 500 milliseconds; machine fails to safe.
